It then addresses maxillary prostheses, focusing on obturator prostheses: their purpose, classification, limitations of defect tissues, tooth engagement principles, design strategies to control movement, and the role of the lateral obturator height. It concludes with a brief description of speech aid prostheses for palatopharyngeal deficiencies.

The section covers surgical preservation strategies that support prosthetic rehabilitation in maxillofacial patients. For maxillary defects, it emphasizes preserving teeth and resecting appropriately, managing the soft palate, skin grafting, and designing or indicating surgery so that definitive or interim obturators can succeed; it also addresses palatal augmentation and preserving tongue mobility. For mandibular defects, it highlights surgical planning to maintain continuity, soft tissue mobility, and function, the trade-offs of reconstruction plates, and the benefits of bone grafts and implants, with the ideal reconstructed mandible providing stable union, contour, attached mucosa, and functional sulci. It also reviews obturator prostheses for maxillary defects, including design, tooth engagement, movement control, and lateral obturator height, and briefly mentions speech aid prostheses for palatopharyngeal deficiencies.

nodes.title: MAXILLARY PROSTHESES
nodes.summary: The text covers prosthodontic considerations in maxillofacial rehabilitation, focusing on mandibular reconstruction requirements and complications, maxillary prostheses (obturators, speech aids, palatal lifts, palatal augmentation), and mandibular resection prostheses. Key points include the importance of soft tissue quality and bone positioning for mandibular reconstruction, the challenges of fibula grafts, classification systems for maxillary and mandibular defects, and design principles for each prosthesis type to achieve stability, retention, and function.

nodes.title: MANDIBULAR PROSTHESES
Evolution of Mandibular Surgical Resection
nodes.summary: The text covers removable partial denture considerations in maxillofacial prosthetics, beginning with tooth arrangement stability and then discussing prostheses for palatopharyngeal incompetence and palatal augmentation. It describes palatal lift prostheses for soft palate paralysis and palatal augmentation prostheses for tongue mobility limitations. The text then addresses mandibular resection prostheses, including the Cantor and Curtis classification, effects of mandibular resection on function, general prosthodontic design principles, and specific design considerations for type I and type II mandibular resections, including framework design, impression techniques, and prosthetic indications.

nodes.title: Type I Resection
nodes.summary: The text discusses prosthetic management after partial mandibulectomy based on the Cantor and Curtis classification. It explains that while reconstruction is now common, when discontinuity defects remain, a mandibular resection prosthesis is needed. General prosthodontic design principles are emphasized, including stress distribution, cross-arch stabilization, and strategic component placement. Type I resections are described as marginal defects with intact inferior border, often designed as Kennedy Class II or IV, with special attention to soft tissue foundation and potential need for labial bars and functional impressions. Type II resections involve segmental defects near the premolar/molar region; prostheses may be needed for tissue support and space filling, with framework design similar to Kennedy Class II, careful abutment stress control, and major connector selection based on functional anatomy.

nodes.title: Type II Resection
nodes.summary: The text covers removable partial denture considerations after partial mandibulectomy using the Cantor and Curtis classification. It explains historical versus current surgical reconstruction, indications for a mandibular resection prosthesis when discontinuity remains, and general prosthodontic framework design principles. It then details prosthodontic management for each defect type: Type I with intact inferior border and Kennedy Class II/IV designs; Type II with premolar/first molar resection, Kennedy Class II framework, retention options, and three-base situations; Type III with half or less mandible remaining and greater dislodgement risk; Type IV based on graft status and extension pattern; and Type V where anterior defects pose airway risk, though the description is incomplete at the end of the provided text.

nodes.title: Mandibular Resection Prosthesis Design: Types III, IV, and V
nodes.summary: This page covers prosthodontic design for mandibular resection defects. It first shows a Type II resection prosthesis and related design principles, including multiple denture base regions, a straight-line rotational axis, broad rest placement, minor connector stability, and wrought-wire retainers. Type III resection, which leaves half or less of the mandible, requires maximal tooth retention and a Type II-like framework, with consideration of alternating retention or Swing-Lock design because of anterior support loss. Type IV resection adapts Type II or III designs depending on the extent of resection, graft characteristics, midline involvement, and TMJ reconstruction. The page ends with the beginning of Type V resection, which concerns involvement of the anterior or posterior denture-bearing area of the mandible.

nodes.title: Type V Resection
nodes.summary: This text covers removable partial denture design considerations for different types of mandibular resections (Types II, III, IV, V) in maxillofacial prosthetics. It details design principles for each type, including support, retention, major connectors, clasps, extension bases, and risk factors. It also discusses the mandibular guide flange prosthesis, emphasizing the uncoordinated movement of the residual mandibular segment due to unilateral muscular activity and the effects of healing. Figures illustrate Type II framework designs, prosthesis placement, and alternating buccal/lingual clasping.

nodes.title: Mandibular Guide Flange Prosthesis
nodes.summary: The text covers removable partial denture considerations in maxillofacial prosthetics, focusing on mandibular resection patients. It describes type II resection designs for different tooth-loss patterns and notes that type V resected mandibles are treated similarly to type I, with soft tissue management at the graft site being the main difference. Conventional clasping with alternating buccal and lingual retention is mentioned. The mandibular guide flange prosthesis is discussed in detail as an interim training device for severe mandibular deviation, including its components, design requirements, retention considerations, and conversion to a definitive prosthesis. Palatal occlusal ramps are presented as an alternative for less severe deviation. Jaw relation records for resection patients require verbal guidance, upright head positioning, and movement toward the nonsurgical side, with an explanation of the compensatory muscle activity involved. The summary emphasizes the challenging, individualized nature of maxillofacial prosthetic treatment and encourages further study of maxillofacial texts.

This section covers prosthodontic management of mandibular prostheses for patients with mandibular resection defects, using the Cantor and Curtis classification. It discusses the evolution from resection to reconstruction, when a mandibular resection prosthesis is indicated, and general framework design principles such as stress distribution, cross-arch stabilization, and strategic component placement. Specific design considerations are provided for Type I (marginal defects with intact inferior border, Kennedy Class II/IV), Type II (segmental premolar/molar defects, Kennedy Class II framework with multiple bases and retention strategies), Type III (half or less of mandible remaining, requiring maximal tooth retention and possible Swing-Lock design), Type IV (design depending on graft, midline, and TMJ status), and Type V (denture-bearing area involvement with graft-site soft tissue management). The section also details the mandibular guide flange prosthesis as an interim training device for severe deviation, palatal occlusal ramps for milder deviation, and jaw relation record techniques. Overall, it emphasizes the individualized and challenging nature of maxillofacial prosthetic treatment.

nodes.title: JAW RELATION RECORDS FOR MANDIBULAR RESECTION PATIENTS
nodes.summary: The text covers removable partial denture considerations in maxillofacial prosthetics, focusing on guide flange prostheses and palatal ramps for mandibular resection patients, including design, retention, conversion to definitive prostheses, and occlusal guidance. It also discusses jaw relation recording for resection patients, emphasizing verbal guidance, proper head positioning, and the compensatory muscle movements enabling lateral excursions. The section concludes with a summary highlighting the individualized and challenging nature of maxillofacial prosthetic treatment.

nodes.title: PHYSIOLOGIC DISTINCTION BETWEEN PROSTHESES
nodes.summary: The text discusses considerations for using dental implants with removable partial dentures, emphasizing the physiologic differences between prostheses. It contrasts support mechanisms and rigidity of fixed prostheses, implant prostheses, and RPDs, and highlights the potential for movement under function and its impact on sensory and functional expectations. It explains the importance of oral sensory input in mastication, the role of periodontal mechanoreceptors, and the loss of guidance precision after tooth loss. Prostheses vary in their ability to compensate for this deficit, depending on how closely they mimic natural teeth and how stable they are under function. The concept of neuromuscular/neurophysiologic ability is introduced, along with patient variability in sensory and motor performance.

nodes.title: REPLACING ANATOMY AND FUNCTIONAL ABILITY

It covers movement control in Class I/II RPDs, implant placement for support vs retention, anatomic limitations in posterior arches, and a comparison between implants and surveyed crowns, emphasizing factors such as support, stability, retention, surgical risk, and long-term maintenance.

nodes.title: STRATEGICALLY PLACED IMPLANTS FOR RPD STABILITY AND IMPROVED PATIENT ACCOMMODATION
nodes.summary: The text covers the use of strategically placed implants to improve removable partial denture stability and patient accommodation, particularly when sensory or neuromuscular deficits make RPD use challenging. It discusses movement control with implants for Kennedy Class I and II prostheses, factors influencing implant placement, the priority of support over retention for comfort, anatomic limitations such as ridge resorption and nearby structures, the uncertain adequacy of short implants, and a comparison between surveyed crowns and implants, highlighting implant advantages in maintenance, attachment accommodation, and variable retention.

nodes.title: SUMMARY
nodes.summary: This chapter discusses considerations for using dental implants with removable partial dentures (RPDs). nodes.title: Dental Prosthodontics Index: L and M Entries and Laboratory Procedures
nodes.summary: This page is an alphabetical index from a dental/dentures text. It continues laboratory-procedure entries and covers the L and M sections, listing page references for lab steps, removable partial denture components, major connectors, mandibular defects/reconstruction, mastication, and materials, and ends with a Telegram link.

nodes.title: L
nodes.summary: The text is an index covering prosthodontic topics. It includes dental materials and alloys, such as metals, metal-ceramic crowns, chromium-cobalt, gold, titanium, tinfoil, VLC, methyl methacrylates, and metallic oxide pastes. It addresses maxillary anatomy, casts, frameworks, major connectors, denture bases, and removable partial dentures. Maxillofacial prosthetics is extensively covered, including defect classification, design considerations, obturators, maxillary and mandibular prostheses, resections, bone grafts, surgical stents, timing of dental care, and potential complications. The text also discusses minor connectors, impression materials, molding/casting procedures, mouth preparation (oral surgical and periodontal), biomechanics of prosthesis movement and stabilization, occlusal relationships and adjustments, mucosal and muscle considerations, molars and modifications, and relevant references and organizations such as Mosby’s Dental Dictionary, Ney surveyors, and NADL.

nodes.title: Dental prosthodontics index: M, N, and O entries
nodes.summary: This page is a dental index covering entries under M, N, and O. It lists topics on prosthesis movement and stability, tissue and muscle considerations, natural teeth support, occlusal adjustments and relationships, oral surgical preparation, oral hygiene and rehabilitation, orthodontic procedures, osseointegration, and treatment outcomes.

nodes.title: O
nodes.summary: This text is an index from a dental reference book, covering topics related to removable partial dentures and prosthodontics. It includes entries on major connectors, path of insertion, patient instructions and interviews, periodontal preparation and surgery, denture bases and relining, impression materials and registration, rests and rest seats, clasp assemblies and retainers, retention, repairs, radiographic examination and interpretation, residual ridge and support, and various prosthodontic treatment considerations.

nodes.title: P
nodes.summary: The text is an index covering removable partial denture and prosthodontic topics, including registration materials, relief spaces, relining/rebasing, remounting, repairs, residual ridge support, resin materials, rests and rest seats, retainers and retention, impression materials, surgical preparation, surveying, stabilization, speech prostheses, laboratory procedures, and clinical care considerations.

nodes.title: Dental Index Entries from Roots to Surveyors
nodes.summary: This page is a dental textbook index covering entries from roots through surveying. It lists R-section topics such as root surgery, rotation, RPA/RPI clasp assemblies, and rugae support, followed by extensive S entries on clinical procedures, impressions, soft tissue, soldering, splinting, stability, stress, major connectors, support, surgical preparation, and surveying. The surgical portion details preprosthetic and maxillofacial procedures, while the surveying section describes types of surveyors, cast handling, and planning placement paths.

nodes.title: S
nodes.summary: This text is an alphabetical index from a dental textbook focused on prosthodontics and removable partial dentures. It lists topics such as surgical preparation, impression techniques, surveying, clasp and retainer design, support and stability, materials, laboratory procedures, treatment planning, and post-insertion care. It also contains a few repeated Telegram join links.

nodes.title: Dental Index: Surveying, T, U, V, and W Topics
nodes.summary: This page indexes dental prosthodontic topics. It includes a continuation of surveyors/surveying entries (survey positions, purposes, tools, cast-surveyor relationships, parallelism, retentive areas, survey line placement, surveyed crowns vs implants, treatment planning, undercut gauges), plus S terms (swallowing, Swing-Lock design, syneresis). The T section covers wires, temporary prostheses, TMJ, tensile strength, connectors, rests, terminology, thermal/impression materials, molars, crowns, tipped abutments, tipping forces, tissue management and health, tooth-supported prostheses, tooth loss/mobility, soldering, tori, trauma, trays, treatment objectives/planning, trial packing, tribochemical coating, reciprocation, tube teeth, tumors, Type I-V resections, and Type IV gold alloys. The U section covers ulcerations, undercuts/undercut gauges, unilateral tooth loss/missing molars, and U-shaped palatal major connectors. The V section covers veneer crowns, vertical axis/movement/path/stresses/support, visible light-cured methods, vitality tests, voids, and V-shaped grooves. The W section covers wax baseplates, blockouts, burnout, impression material, indicators, interocclusal records, and ledges. A link to a dental books Telegram channel is appended.

nodes.title: V
nodes.summary: The text is an index from a removable partial prosthodontics textbook. It covers surveying and surveyors, prosthesis designs and components, dental materials and their properties, tooth and abutment evaluation, tissue management, biomechanics, major connectors and denture bases, treatment planning and phases of service, surgical and pathological conditions, laboratory and record procedures, implants, and miscellaneous clinical topics such as xerostomia, tooth loss, and unilateral missing molars.

nodes.title: Dental Prosthodontics Index Entries W, X, Y, Z
nodes.summary: This index page lists dental prosthodontic entries under W, X, Y, and Z, covering waxing techniques and materials, framework and denture-base procedures, wedging, facebows, work authorizations, wrought-wire components, titanium alloy properties, xerostomia, and zinc oxide-eugenol impression paste, with figure and page references.

structure.summary: This section is a complete alphabetical index from a dental textbook on removable partial dentures and prosthodontics. It lists page, figure, box, and table references for topics from A to Z, serving as a navigational tool. The index covers prosthodontic components and designs, biomechanics, clinical diagnosis and treatment planning, surgical and implant considerations, maxillofacial prosthetics, laboratory procedures, dental materials and alloys, infection control, tissue management, and a wide range of related clinical and technical terms.
